recentItems.title: Senior Houthi official warns countries against joining Saudi Arabia in Yemen’s revived civil war
recentItems.description:
(21 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

++STARTS AND ENDS ON SOUNDBITES++
++VIA VIDEO CALL++ 

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Sanaa, Yemen - 20 September 2026
1. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, Member of the Houthis’ political bureau: 
“Recently, there was an American communication through the Omani mediator if we would target America (in) Bab el-Mandab. We confirmed that we are not targeting America, or any other country, in the strait, with the sole exception of the Saudi enemy.”
++WHITE FLASH++
2. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, Member of the Houthis’ political bureau:
“Reaching Bab el-Mandab Strait was not an objective in itself; rather, it was a consequence of Saudi Arabia igniting internal fronts to relieve pressure on itself—a move that ultimately cost it that strategic card.”
++WHITE FLASH++
3. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, Member of the Houthis’ political bureau: 
“The balance of power shifted in favor of the Sanaa government (The Houthi de facto authorities in the Yemeni capital), and this explains the rapid resolution of the conflict on the Western Coast. Today, Yemen is capable of waging battle on three fronts, one regional front and that is the Saudi enemy, which we choose in order to end the war on Yemen and the (Saudi) blockade. We were also prepared for an internal conflict with any mercenaries associated with Saudi Arabia. We are even ready for an international front should any nation become implicated in the aggression against Yemen alongside Saudi Arabia.”
++ENDS ON SOUNDBITE++
STORYLINE:
A senior official with the Iran-backed Houthi rebels is warning countries against joining Saudi Arabia in Yemen’s revived civil war, telling The Associated Press on Sunday that his group has assured the Trump administration that it won’t attack U.S. vessels in the Red Sea.

Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, member of the Houthis’ political bureau, said the U.S. administration has contacted the rebels via Oman to inquire whether the Houthis plan to target U.S. assets in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait after their sweeping advance down Yemen’s western coast earlier this month.

“We confirmed that we are not targeting the United States, or any other nation, in the strait, with the sole exception of the Saudi enemy,” he told the AP in a Zoom interview from the rebel-held Yemeni capital, Sanaa. “That remains the case.”

U.S. President Donald Trump last week said his administration has “had discussions” with the Houthis, but did not say when. “The Houthis called us, and they don’t want to fight with us,” he said. “They would much prefer not having us involved, and they’re letting most ships go through.”

AP later reported that Oman hosted a meeting between U.S. and Houthi representatives last weekend, citing a Houthi official and another individual familiar with the talks. They spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren’t authorized to brief the media.

However, al-Bukhaiti only confirmed indirect contacts with U.S. officials through longtime mediator Oman, which brokered a 2025 ceasefire between the Houthis and the Trump administration. That ended a weeks-long U.S. air campaign against the rebels in return for them ceasing attacks on U.S. vessels in the Red Sea.

Al-Bukhaiti said the rebels have the capacity to fight a multiple-front war, “should any nation become implicated in the aggression against Yemen alongside Saudi Arabia.”





The U.S., which bombed the Houthis under the Biden and Trump administrations, has shown no interest in getting involved militarily this time around.

recentItems.title: Village in northeastern Afghanistan heavily damaged in night-time Pakistani airstrikes
recentItems.description:
(21 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY: NO ACCESS AFGHANISTAN INTERNATIONAL

ASSOCIATED PRESS - NO ACCESS AFGHANISTAN INTERNATIONAL
Nurgul District, Kunar Province - 21 September 2026
1. Left pan aftermath of Pakistani air strikes, villagers around
2. Close up of broken household items
3. Various of villager searching for belongings
4. Close of a sandal lying on debris 
5. SOUNDBITE (Pashto) Samar Gul, relative of the victims:
“Last night at 3:00 am, Pakistani jet aircraft bombed this area, killing our fellow villagers. We arrived here at 3:30am; we transported the wounded to the hospital and recovered the bodies of the martyrs from the debris. This is a grave atrocity committed by Pakistan, an act of cruelty that has no place in Islam or anywhere else in the world. We call upon the international community to investigate such incidents.”
6. Various of destroyed house, villagers around
7. SOUNDBITE  (Pashto) Abdul Hanan, resident of Nurgal District:
“It was 3:30 when aircraft bombed us, and we found ourselves facing this tragedy. It was a truly heartbreaking situation, brother. We urge that, whenever such things happen, cooperation and assistance be provided to the affected people. Within a radius of about twenty or thirty meters, the village is devastated; trees, shrubs, houses, and many other things were destroyed.”
9. Various of destruction, debris, scattered belongings
STORYLINE:
Pakistani jet fighters carried out airstrikes Monday on what security officials described as suspected militant hideouts in eastern Afghanistan and claimed 28 of them were killed. 

Authorities in Kabul said at least three people were killed.

“This is a grave atrocity committed by Pakistan, an act of cruelty that has no place in Islam or anywhere else in the world. We call upon the international community to investigate such incidents," said Samar Gul, relative of the victims. 

The strikes near the frontier between the two countries marked a renewed escalation between Pakistan and Afghanistan, raising the prospect of further cross-border hostilities and threatening to complicate efforts by regional countries including China to mediate between Islamabad and Kabul. 

They came after Pakistan warned it could target militants inside Afghanistan following two deadly attacks in recent days on its security forces near the border. 

Militant attacks targeting Pakistan’s police and security forces have surged in recent years. 

The escalation follows months of military action. 

Hundreds of people have been killed in cross-border fighting since February, when Afghanistan launched retaliatory strikes after Pakistan carried out airstrikes inside Afghan territory.

Authorities in Islamabad have blamed the Pakistani Taliban and allied militant groups for most of the violence. 

The Pakistani Taliban are separate from but allied with the Afghan Taliban that returned to power in 2021.

Two Pakistani security officials said 28 suspected militants were killed in Monday's airstrikes. 

Afghanistan’s government, however, said the strikes killed three civilians and wounded four others. The claims from either side could not immediately be independently verified.

The Pakistani officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly. Pakistan’s military did not immediately issue a statement on the strikes.

In a post on X, Afghan Taliban government spokesman Zabiullah Mujahid condemned the airstrikes and said there would be a response.

ASSOCIATED PRESS
London, UK - 20 September 2026

1. Various of Pearly Queens shaking hands with the crowd, band plays music in the background 
2. Mid of Pearly King singing Daisy Bell (written in 1892)

If someone doesn't know who you are, maybe you know you'll get a few who is the nutter in the buttons, but usually it's a smile and oh it's a Pearly. We are a bit of a rare breed, I suppose now that London's grown so big."

8. Rear view of Pearly Queens in feather hats watching Morris dancers performing
9. Tilt down of waistcoat with thousands of buttons sewn in

"On the average suit of buttons there are about 2,000 to 3,000 buttons. And they're also sewn on by hand. You can't put them on by machine. And just to give you an idea, just in this section here, it's 350 buttons."

12. Mid tilt down from Maypole
13. Wide of Pearly Queens Maypole dancing with City of London mayoral dignitaries 
14. Various set up shots of Evie Waldren, Pearly Queen of Barnet showing her outfit
15. SOUNDBITE: (Backslang and English) Evie Waldren, Pearly Queen of Barnet
"SPEAKING BACKSLANG"
"So I just said, hello. My name is Evie, and I'm the Pearly Queen of Barnet."

16. Wide of Evie Waldren singing Daisy Bell
17. SOUNDBITE: (Backslang and English) Evie Waldren, Pearly Queen of Barnet
"Once you get the knack, you can say any word. I could say microwave. I could say supercalifragilistic in it, because you know the code."
Reporter: "Say supercalifragilisticexpialidocious"
"Oh god, I've set myself up here...  Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious (IN BACKSLANG)"

18. Various set up shots of John Scott, Pearly King of Mile End
19. SOUNDBITE: (English) John Scott, Pearly King of Mile End
"Could you point at the camera man... from the shoulder to the wrist is a Chalk Farm (arm). From the wrist to the fingertips, it's either the Camber Sand or the German band (hand). Could you put your German band on your fish and chip (hip) please? Right this bit here, there is no rhyming slang for it, but I'll tell you what I call it. I call it the Spanish Archer. Spanish archer? El bow. You can put it down there now. Now we're going to move up above the shoulders, above the shoulders and below the head is a bushel and peck, neck. Above the bushel and peck is a loaf of bread, head. On the top of the loaf of bread you've got the Barnet Fair (hair). Unless, of course, you've got alopecia or something like that. Then you'd wear a syrup of fig (wig)."

20. Mid of John Scott showing his Proud to be Born a Cockney waistcoat
21. Wide of Conor singing Don't Dilly Dally on the Way (written in 1919)
22. Mid of Conor Cranston-Scott (second right) with his grandad John Scott (far right) and his father Terry Scott (second left) showing three generations of Pearlies

recentItems.title: Germany's far-right AfD leaders believe state election results show they have path to replacing CDU
recentItems.description:
(21 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Berlin - 21 September 2026
1. AfD co-leaders Tino Chrupalla and Alice Weidel arriving for news conference
2. Wide of AfD co-leaders Tino Chrupalla and Alice Weidel at podium, surrounded by cameras and photographers
3. SOUNDBITE (German) Alice Weidel, AfD co-leader:
"As the Alternative for Germany, we have achieved excellent election results in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and in Berlin. And especially in Berlin, considering that the Left Party has essentially absorbed the entire camp, achieving 16% here is an outstanding result. And in Berlin, a very clear trend is emerging that we will replace the CDU."
4. Wide of news conference
5. Cutaway of a journalist
6. SOUNDBITE (German) Alice Weidel, AfD co-leader:
"This is the second consecutive state election victory for the Alternative for Germany, which of course makes us incredibly happy as a party. And it clearly shows that we have replaced the CDU as the people's party, which for the first time in its history is no longer represented in a parliament at all. This is also the result of a very unintelligent firewall policy, and the CDU must decide how it wants to proceed now."
7. Wide of news conference
8. SOUNDBITE (German) Tino Chrupalla, AfD co-leader
++STARTS WITH ALICE WEIDEL++
"Perhaps just briefly to add regarding the CDU and the destruction. The CDU... it’s not our job to destroy it. Voters decided that in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. And I would also like to dispel the notion of portraying the CDU as conservative. The CDU is pseudo-conservative; it is no longer conservative. It also does not pursue conservative policies, as it has completely distanced itself from conservatism, aligning with the Left Party and the SPD, as can be seen at the federal level."
9. Wide of news conference
STORYLINE:
Germany's far-right AfD leaders on Monday said they believed regional election results show they have a path to replacing the center-right Christian Democratic Union. 

Alternative for Germany, or AfD, co-leaders Alice Weidel and Tino Chrupalla said the party had achieved "excellent results" over the weekend. 

"We have achieved excellent election results in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and in Berlin. And especially in Berlin, considering that the Left Party has essentially absorbed the entire camp, achieving 16% here is an outstanding result," she said. 

"It clearly shows that we have replaced the CDU as the people's party," she added. 

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz faces a struggle to stabilize his position and keep his agenda on track after voters inflicted two more defeats on his party, ejecting it from a state legislature for the first time.

Merz vowed to stay on and push through reforms to Germany minutes after polls closed Sunday in regional elections in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, a largely rural eastern region on the Baltic Sea coast.

Still, final results underlined the extent of what Merz conceded was a “disaster” in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. 

Neither state is one of Germany's political heavyweights. The CDU's 2023 win in Berlin was its only one in the past 25 years in the capital, which has tended to lean left, and the party was already weak in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.

But the manner of its defeat in the latter in particular adds to the headwinds Merz faces after a stinging defeat by the AfD two weeks ago in Saxony-Anhalt, another region in the formerly communist east, damaged his authority and set off speculation that he might be replaced.



AP video by: Pietro De Cristofaro

recentItems.title: SIRIA: Una exposición revisita las prisiones de la era de Assad a través de objetos dejados por los
recentItems.description:
(21 Sep 2026) 
SLUG: Siria Prisiones (SP)
Source: ASSOCIATED PRESS
No additional restrictions beyond those terms outlined in your license agreement.
Video de AP realizado por Ghaith Alsayed.

SIRIA: Una exposición revisita las prisiones de la era de Assad a través de objetos dejados por los detenidos

—————————————————————————————————————-
ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Damasco, Siria - 31 de agosto de 2026

El Ministerio del Interior de Siria  ha presentado, en la Feria Internacional del mes de agosto, una exposición llamada "Cuando las paredes hablan", que muestra objetos de prisiones y cuerpos de seguridad que operaron bajo el régimen del expresidente Bashar al-Assad.

La exposición incluyó puertas de celdas llenas de escritos de prisioneros, ropa, llaves perdidas, esposas oxidadas y prótesis, y objetos que, según el ministerio, se usaban para torturar a los detenidos. 

El pabellón estuvo muy concurrido pero para algunos visitantes era más que una exposición. 

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Damasco, Siria - 1 de septiembre de 2026 

SOUNDBITE (Árabe) Abdul Wahab Yasser, familiar de un exrecluso: 
“No hay palabras para describir el dolor”, dijo este familiar de un exrecluso. “Quienes quieran venir aquí deben tener la capacidad de soportar”.

SOUNDBITE (Arabe) Abdul Wahab Yasser, familiar de un exrecluso: 
“Mi primo murió en la comisaria de Kfar Sousse”, dijo este familiar. “Vine aquí esperando ver su nombre en las paredes, pero no lo encontré”.

 ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Damasco, Siria - 31 de agosto de 2026

La exposición se inauguró menos de dos años después de que las fuerzas rebeldes derrocaran a Assad en diciembre de 2024, y abrieran las prisiones del país.

Siria aún lucha por recuperarse tras 14 años de guerra civil que dejaron un saldo estimado de medio millón de muertos, millones de desplazados y un país devastado y dividido.

SOUNDBITE (Arabe) Walid al-Hussein, de la Dirección General de Prisiones y Centros Penitenciarios del Ministerio del Interior de Siria: 
“Aspiramos a cambiar, en un futuro próximo, la filosofía punitiva de matar y torturar a los detenidos —que seguía el antiguo régimen— por un nuevo sistema que salvaguarde la dignidad humana del recluso  ”, dijo este funcionario sirio.

En un informe publicado en marzo, la Comisión Internacional Independiente de Investigación de la ONU sobre la República Árabe Siria declaró haber documentado "torturas y malos tratos" en 18 centros de detención oficiales y 12 "centros improvisados" en Siria entre enero y octubre de 2025, cuando el nuevo gobierno consolidó su control.

ANNE MARIE GARCIA, ASSOCIATED PRESS
STORYLINE:
Una antigua celda, tenuemente iluminada y sucia, tiene colchones delgados esparcidos por el suelo. Ropa manchada y pertenencias personales cuelgan del techo, mientras nombres y otros escritos cubren las paredes.

La celda reconstruida forma parte de “Cuando hablan las paredes”, una exposición organizada por el Ministerio del Interior de Siria en la Feria Internacional de Damasco. La muestra reúne objetos procedentes de prisiones y dependencias de seguridad que operaron durante el gobierno del expresidente Bashar Assad.

Entre las piezas hay puertas cubiertas con mensajes de prisioneros, ropa, llaves, esposas oxidadas, prótesis y objetos que, según el ministerio, fueron utilizados para torturar a detenidos.

Para algunos visitantes, el pabellón es un lugar donde buscan rastros de familiares desaparecidos durante el régimen de Assad.

Abdul Wahab Yasser acudió con la esperanza de encontrar una señal de su primo, quien, según dijo, murió en la dependencia de seguridad de Kfar Sousse.

recentItems.title: Monet masterpiece could sell for record €30 million
recentItems.description:
(21 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Paris, France - 17 September 2026
1. Various of Claude Monet, Iris, 1924-25, displayed at Sotheby’s auction house in Paris
2. SOUNDBITE (French) Marianne Mathieu, Historian of Impressionism, Director of the Nymphéas project (WPI) and former Scientific Director of the Musée Marmottan-Monet: 
"To truly discover and understand it, this material needs to be preserved. And we can still see these impasto brushstrokes. The painting has never been damaged or varnished. When you varnish a painting, you change its chromatic tones. All of this means that today we are discovering a painting that is classic, exemplary of what Monet would have wanted to show us. It is truly an absolutely moving, important and rare discovery. It is really a moment of total emotion."
3. Various of paintings by Monet 
4. SOUNDBITE (English) Thomas Bompard, Co-Head of Modern and Contemporary Art at Sotheby’s France:
"This is a collection that many people knew the existence of but really only a few people were able to see the paintings. It’s an extraordinary collection given the calibre and the quality of the works leading this collection - two incredible Monet, shown to the public for the very first time. And it’s also an extraordinary collection given the personality of the main architect of this collection - Jeanne Schlumberger - the wife of the founder of the Schlumberger group."
5. Various of paintings by Monet 
STORYLINE:
Purple, white and green brushstrokes merge in Claude Monet's 'Iris'.

The Impressionist painting is displayed for the first time in public, on the walls of the Sotheby's gallery in Paris.

It will go up for sale next month.

Sotheby's has listed it with an estimate of 22 to 30 million euros (25 to 34 million USD) - the highest valuation ever assigned to a painting at auction in France. 

For Marianne Mathieu, a historian of Impressionism, the painting is “absolutely moving, important and a rare discovery”. 

“The painting has never been damaged or varnished. When you varnish a painting, you change its chromatic tones. All of this means that today we are discovering a painting that is classic, exemplary of what Monet would have wanted to show us,” says Mathieu.

It’s part of 'Le Temps Retrouvé: The Schlumberger' collection.

It was assembled over more than five decades by Jeanne Schlumberger, part of a wealthy French family.

The art she gathered has an overall estimate of more than 40 million euros.

Iris is joined by other works of Monet, including Saule pleureur (est. €8-12 million), part of the artist’s series of paintings depicting weeping willows in his Giverny garden painted in the aftermath of the First World War. 

All the Monets are displayed to the public for the first time. 

Le Temps Retrouvé features 28 works overall, including from artists Paul Cézanne, Gustave Moreau and Camille Claudel.

For art journalist Emma Louise Diest, having them out in public is a new chapter for the work

It’s been hidden for so many years, and it had a story there but nobody could join that story, could be part of it. And now there’s a new story written," she says.

Buyers will bid for the collection during Sotheby’s Live Evening auction on 22 October.

AP video shot by Elitsa Gadeva

AGENCY POOL

10. Banner of 2026 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance 
11. Wide of conference

STORYLINE:
U.S. President Donald Trump and China's leader Xi Jinping are expected to meet this week as competition over the technology intensifies.

The two are leaders of rival nations in a race to dominate artificial intelligence.

Their meeting comes during growing concerns about AI safety after American AI leaders, led by Anthropic’s CEO, called for a global slowdown in AI development.

The hopes for finding common ground on concerns around global AI safety are clouded by competition between the two countries. 

As China narrows the technology gap with the U.S., each country has expressed concern over how AI in the other's hands could hurt them.

On Sunday, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said after talks in New York with China's Vice Premier He Lifeng ahead of the meeting between Trump and Xi that the two countries discussed the setting up of a mechanism on AI dialogue and proposed a new “notification mechanism” for AI incidents that could impact national security.
